connector.modeled: Owner decision 2026-11-05: no SMA/coax; 50 ohm vertical AddLumpedPort at the line start (board edge y=-13), strip width, R=50 ohm; S11 reference plane = line start, no de-embedding (run with --edge-port lumped). Feed: 50 ohm line (w 3.92 mm, y -13 -> -9.801) + lambda/4 transformer (w 0.80 mm, l 6.60 mm) touching the radiating edge y=-3.201 (no inset, no notch). US3_PS4: patch_L 6.502 -> 6.402 (patch edge -3.251 -> -3.201); the 0.80 x 6.60 mm transformer keeps its length and the 50 ohm section absorbs the 0.05 mm (3.149 -> 3.199 mm); port at y=-13 and S11 reference plane unchanged.

feed.line_width_method: Hammerstad-Jensen (with Wheeler 35 um thickness correction) on eps_r 4.4, h 2.07 mm: w = 3.919 mm -> 3.92 mm gives Z0 = 49.99 ohm, eps_eff = 3.308 (estimate, GEOMETRY_ONLY)
feed.transformer_width_method: Hammerstad-Jensen static Z0 (Wheeler 35 um correction): w 0.80 mm -> Zt 102.5 ohm; Kirschning-Jansen eps_eff(f0) 3.197 (GUIDE_MODEL)

parasitic_params.note: Floating sheet (no via, no probe), same metal as the patch. Lp 7.6 -> 7.67 mm about the SAME centre y = 0.80 mm as US3_PS1 (each end +0.035 mm). The polygon stays inside y >= -3.035 so it does not lie under the 0.8 mm transformer / 50 ohm line: the patch edge is now y = -3.201 (patch_L/2), the transformer ends there on z = h, and the sheet (z = 1.035) starts 0.166 mm above it in y. y_min = -3.0 (PS1 value) gave a y grading ratio 1.853 > 1.5 in prepare (patch edge -3.201 and sheet edge -3.0 only 0.2 mm apart); -3.035 and -2.95 pass, -2.975 does not.

US3_PS1.note: JUSTIFIED EXCEPTION (two simultaneous changes, patch_L and Lp). Owner objective 2026-11-15: raise the main (lower) mode a little and keep the upper one (~8.03 GHz) where it is. The two modes are hybrids of the excited patch and the parasitic, so a single dimension moves BOTH; holding the upper mode needs a differential move (patch_L shorter = patch frequency up; Lp longer = parasitic frequency down). Everything else (patch width, U-slot, 50 ohm line width, transformer 0.80 x 6.60 mm, parasitic width 11.0 mm, z = 1.035 mm, FR4, board, metal, port) is identical to US3_PS1. The U-slot is NOT moved with the patch edges (absolute coordinates kept), so slot-to-edge copper is 1.251 mm (+y) and 2.501 mm (-y).

rationale: Owner request 2026-11-15 (second version): from US3_PS1 (rounds 031/032: S11 minima -31.7 dB at 7.675 GHz and -25.4 dB at 8.03 GHz, worst in channel -5.96 dB at 8.2368 GHz, eta 0.64 -> 0.225 (f0) -> 0.515) raise the main resonance a little and keep the second where it is, to bring both closer from below. MODE IDENTIFICATION (not unambiguous, see computation): two arguments on the 032 data point in opposite directions, hence the identification is NOT settled. (1) Critical-coupling argument (both S11 minima are within -25 dB of a match, i.e. the port external rate ~ the unloaded rate of each mode) with Q_u = Q_d*(1-eta) (Q_d = 1/tan_delta = 58.8, eta at the mode from the NF2FF points) gives a port-coupled (driven-patch) energy weight of ~0.67 in the lower mode (range 0.55-0.80): lower mode = excited-patch-dominated, upper mode = parasitic-dominated (weight ~0.67), antiphase 'dark' mode (radiation Q ~200 vs ~33). This also fits the PS1 guide (parasitic alone ~8.06 GHz +-4 %, here ~7.92) and the owner's original reading. (2) Frequency-sum argument (f1^2 + f2^2 conserved under symmetric coupling, driven patch alone at its US3_MS3 openEMS value 7.95-7.98 GHz) gives the opposite: lower mode parasitic-dominated (driven weight ~0.24, parasitic alone ~7.75 GHz). It only holds if the parasitic does not pull the driven patch down; (1) needs it to be pulled down by ~0.15-0.2 GHz. Working choice: (1), the better-supported one (it uses the radiation and port-coupling data, not an assumption on the unperturbed patch), with a ~60 % confidence by judgement; PS4 itself is the discriminating experiment (the signs of the f1 and f2 shifts differ between the two). CHOICE: patch_L 6.502 -> 6.402 mm (-0.10 mm, inside the owner's HFSS patch_L sweep 6.402-6.502) raises the patch frequency by ~71 MHz (7.06 MHz per 0.01 mm); Lp 7.60 -> 7.67 mm (+0.07 mm) lowers the parasitic frequency by ~68 MHz (9.7 MHz per 0.01 mm). The sum is a DETUNING REDUCTION (patch_L up/Lp down in frequency) that, for the identification (1), raises the lower mode at fixed upper mode. LIMIT (the important caveat): the two modes are already close to the coupling-limited minimum separation (2*c/(f1+f2) ~ 0.33 GHz for w = 0.67 versus 0.355 GHz now; 0.28-0.35 GHz over w 0.55-0.80). With coupling unchanged the lower mode can rise by at most ~+2 (w 0.55), +22 (w 0.67) or +72 MHz (w 0.80) with the upper mode fixed; the chosen move gives ~+12 MHz (range -5 to +32). That is of the order of the mesh uncertainty (~13 MHz, round 031). A larger rise of the main mode needs EITHER the upper mode to rise with it (shift of the whole pair, e.g. patch_L -0.10 alone: +45/+26 MHz, which moves the eta valley to ~8.06 GHz inside the channel) OR a smaller coupling k (z_par, overlap), not a size change. Not changed: z_par, Wp, U-slot, transformer, port. GEOMETRY_ONLY; no S11, gain, efficiency or bandwidth is claimed.

computation.label: GUIDE_MODEL (coupled-mode f^2 matrix calibrated with openEMS 032; NOT EM, no result for PS4)
computation.method: (a) Mode frequencies of 032 taken at the S11 minima (7.675 and 8.03 GHz; Re(Zin) peaks 7.64/8.045 give the same trace within 0.1 %). (b) 2x2 coupled-mode matrix M = [[fa^2, c],[c, fb^2]], fa = excited patch, fb = parasitic, eigenvalues f1^2, f2^2 = 7.675^2, 8.03^2. The driven-patch energy weight w of the lower mode fixes the matrix (fa^2 = w f1^2 + (1-w) f2^2, fb^2 = (1-w) f1^2 + w f2^2, c = sqrt(w(1-w)) (f2^2 - f1^2)). (c) w from the critical-coupling/eta argument: kappa_e,i = w_i kappa_e (external rate of mode i = driven-patch weight x rate of the patch), matched minima -> kappa_e,i ~ kappa_u,i = f_i/Q_u,i, Q_u,i = Q_d (1 - eta_i) with Q_d = 58.8 (tan_delta 0.017, metal loss neglected, field in air neglected) and eta_1 = 0.64 (7.7376 GHz, nearest NF2FF point to the lower mode), eta_2 = 0.225 (7.9872 GHz; 0.24 at 8.037): Q_u = 21 and 45 -> w_2/w_1 = 0.49 -> w = 0.67. The result is the weight of the excited patch in the lower mode and rests on both minima being near critical coupling (S11 -31.7/-25.4 dB), which is only approximately true because the lambda/4 transformer and the 50 ohm line sit between the port and the patch edge. (d) Shifts: d fa = +7.06 MHz per -0.01 mm of patch_L (owner HFSS sweep 7.0 MHz/0.01 mm in the HFSS frame x 1.009 openEMS frame, hfss/hfss_parametric_patch_L_2026-11-13.json); d fb = -9.7 MHz per +0.01 mm of Lp (the 9.6 MHz of the US3_PS1 guide x 1.009; the guide's own formula slope check: f/L_eff = 7.92/8.53 -> 9.3 MHz per 0.01 mm). These slopes are NOT calibrated with 031/032: those two runs have one geometry, so no slope can be derived from them; what was calibrated with 032 are the mode frequencies, the weights and the coupling c. A slope error of +-20 % moves the predicted shifts by about +-3 MHz. Circuit-fit attempt: a 2-resonator + microstrip-transformer fit of the 032 (and 023) Zin did NOT converge to a physical solution (parameters ran into the bounds; residual ~0.15 in |Gamma| even for the single-patch US3_MS3), so no fit result is used; the identification relies only on (c) and the sum rule.

inputs.US3_MS3_023_single_resonance_ghz: S11 min -16.2 dB at 7.999, Re(Zin) peak 69 ohm at ~7.93-7.95 (port plane)

outputs.expected_effect_on_S11_channel: NOT predicted: the model has no S11. Judgement: with the upper mode (which sets the -5.96 dB at 8.2368 GHz) almost fixed and f1 +~12 MHz, the change of the worst-in-channel value is expected to be small (<~0.5 dB); the upper-edge -6 dB is not expected to be secured by this move alone.
outputs.expected_effect_on_eta: The ~8.0 GHz dark mode stays in the channel (valley expected 0.2-0.3 around 7.98-8.04 GHz); H2 is expected to FAIL (eta >= 0.55 at all 11 points) unless the loss mechanism is something else than the mode character.
outputs.uncertainty: identification ~60/40 (B/A); f1, f2 shifts of the chosen move are below or of the order of the mesh uncertainty (~13 MHz) in B and clear (~40 MHz, opposite signs) in A.

pre_registered_hypothesis.H1: Same solver/mesh as 032 (openEMS base, --max-timesteps 60000). Worst |S11| over the 7.7376-8.2368 GHz grid of 1 MHz <= -8 dB (preferred -10 dB; the -6 dB minimum reference being the pass line for 'no worse than a usable match'). Guide expectation (judgement, not a result): -6.0 to -6.5 dB, i.e. H1 is expected to FAIL; the guide predicts the upper edge to be limited by the upper (~8.03 GHz) mode, which this variant keeps. Mode shifts to be read from the run: B (excited-patch-dominated lower mode) predicts f1 +12 MHz (-5..+32) and f2 -9 MHz (+8..-29); A (parasitic-dominated lower mode) predicts f1 -42 and f2 +45 MHz.
pre_registered_hypothesis.H2: eta (Prad/Pacc) >= 0.55 at ALL 11 NF2FF points of the channel AND realized broadside gain >= 2 dBi at all 11 points (032: eta 0.225 and -0.61 dBi at f0; 8.037 GHz -0.78 dBi). Central risk: the eta valley (0.225) is tied to the ~8.03 GHz mode; if this mode remains in the channel (expected), S11 can improve while eta and realized gain get worse or stay: a match by LOSS (antiphase mode radiating poorly, dissipating in the FR4 tan_delta 0.017). H2 is expected to FAIL; an S11 gain with an eta valley is NOT counted as an improvement.
pre_registered_hypothesis.decision_rule: (1) H1 true and H2 true: fine-mesh run (two-mesh convergence), then owner decision on HFSS and design-reviewer. (2) H1 true, H2 false (match by loss): US3_PS4 is NOT a candidate; do not spend refinement 2 on size; the line (buried parasitic with homogeneous FR4) stays rejected for gain/efficiency; the remaining lever is a loss control (tan_delta = 0 on the same geometry, a diagnostic, not a design). (3) H1 false and f1 rose / f2 fixed within +-15 MHz (identification B confirmed, as predicted): the size lever is exhausted by the coupling-limited separation; refinement 2 (last) = reduce coupling k (z_par moved off h/2, e.g. 0.80 mm; or Wp) to bring the modes closer, NOT another size change; or shift the whole pair (patch_L -0.10 alone) only if the owner accepts the eta valley moving inside the channel. (4) H1 false and f1 fell / f2 rose (identification A): the sign of both changes was wrong; refinement 2 = the reverse differential (patch_L longer by ~0.05..0.10 mm, Lp shorter by ~0.07 mm) or accept that the modes are separated and move to the upper-edge fix by raising the upper mode. (5) Shifts inside the mesh uncertainty (<13 MHz) in both modes: no information; do NOT repeat a micro-change; take the coupling option of (3) as refinement 2.
pre_registered_hypothesis.evidence_rule: Nothing here is a result. One FDTD base-mesh run of US3_PS4 only tests these hypotheses. Max 2 refinements per candidate: this is refinement 1 of US3_PS1 (the first was not taken). Refinement 2 (last) remains.

manufacturability.layers: 3 copper layers (L1 patch + feed + U-slot at z=h, L2 floating parasitic at z=1.035 mm, L3 ground at z=0) and 2 dielectric layers of ~1.035 mm each: a standard 3-copper-layer FR4 multilayer (core + prepreg/core).
manufacturability.vias: none: the parasitic is floating (no probe, no plated through hole in the antenna region); the feed is a planar microstrip.
manufacturability.min_feature_mm: U-slot arms 0.8 mm and gaps as in US3_MS3 (unchanged); parasitic is a solid rectangle 11.0 x 7.6 mm, no feature < 0.8 mm.
manufacturability.stackup_note: Dielectric thickness and the exact z of the buried copper depend on the fabricator's core/prepreg library; typical core thicknesses of ~1.0-1.2 mm and prepreg of 0.1-0.2 mm are only an orientation (NOT verified against a datasheet). The model assumes ONE homogeneous eps_r=4.4 over 2.07 mm, so the fabricator must give the real stackup (the prepreg/core eps_r can differ from the core and sets z_par and k).
manufacturability.tolerances_to_specify: layer-to-layer registration and dielectric thickness ( +-z_par moves k and f2 ); etching of Lp (guide: ~10 MHz per 0.01 mm). Same rough FR4 + copper-roughness caveat as the rest of the campaign.
manufacturability.risks: z_par and registration are not controlled by the TFG; the model is homogeneous FR4 (provisional); a floating inner sheet cannot be seen or tuned after lamination. US3_PS4: the two size changes are 0.10 mm (patch_L) and 0.07 mm (Lp), of the order of the etching tolerance (guide ~7-10 MHz per 0.01 mm): a +-0.05 mm etching error moves the modes by ~35-50 MHz, larger than the predicted effect of the change.

purpose: Test, in openEMS base mesh, whether a differential detuning (patch_L -0.10 mm, Lp +0.07 mm) raises the main resonance of US3_PS1 with the 8.03 GHz mode fixed, and whether the eta valley tied to the 8.03 GHz mode follows the S11 improvement (match by loss).
mesh_hint_note: Hard y line at -0.215 mm (inside the U-slot base, as US3_MS3/US3_PS1). Prepare-only trials for US3_PS4 (base mesh, round-32 command): with the PS1 sheet edge y_min = -3.0 the y grading ratio was 1.853 > 1.5 near lines -3.2843, -3.201 (patch edge), -3.0466; the fix was to move the sheet edge (y_min = -3.035, ratio 1.4) instead of adding hints: hints at -3.1/-3.12/-3.3 did not fix it or gave 1.56.
